subject: Life Skills
title: The 30-Day Rule
description: A micro-lesson that makes The 30-Day Rule usable.

hook.text: He saw a drone online, added it to his cart, and forced himself to wait 30 days. He never went back.

buildup.text: The 30-day rule says: write down any non-essential purchase you want and wait. If you still want it in 30 days, buy it.

discovery.text: Most impulse desires fade within a week. The dopamine spike from wanting is gone and rational evaluation takes over.

twist.text: If you still want it after 30 days, the purchase is probably worthwhile. The rule does not ban spending — it filters it.

climax.text: Keep a 'want list' on your phone. Date each entry. Review the list monthly.

punchline.text: Wait 30 days. Most wants expire on their own.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the 30-day rule?
options: To save money by never buying non-essentials
To filter impulse purchases by letting the initial desire fade naturally
To budget for large purchases over multiple months
